meta.name: Assess GitHub bus-factor risk in GitHub with Claude, tickets and Slack

name: AI Code Ownership & Bus-Factor Intelligence Engine

parameters.content:
## AI Code Ownership & Bus-Factor Intelligence Engine

### How it works

This workflow ingests GitHub push events, pull-request merges, and a periodic contributor-stats baseline scan, normalizes them into a shared ownership-signal format, and stores them in a temporary ownership buffer. On a scheduled batch window, it retrieves recent buffered signals, computes commit-concentration scores per repo/component, and pre-clusters them into clearly healthy, clearly critical, or ambiguous groups. Claude is only used to judge the ambiguous groups (borderline ownership concentration where context matters); clear cases pass straight through. The resolved clusters are turned into knowledge-transfer/documentation tasks, pushed into a ticketing system, and announced to engineering leadership in Slack.

### Setup steps

- Configure GitHub webhooks (push and pull_request events) on the relevant repositories to point at the two webhook triggers below.
- Add a GitHub API credential (header auth / PAT) to the Fetch Org Repositories and Fetch Contributor Stats HTTP Request nodes, and set your org name in the repositories URL.
- Review and adapt each normalization Code node so the incoming payload shapes map to the same canonical fields: source, repo, component, contributor, commit counts, and timestamp.
- Add credentials and endpoint details for the ownership-signal buffer API used by the store and fetch HTTP Request nodes.
- Set the Cron/baseline schedule to how often you want a full contributor-stats scan, and set the batch-window schedule to how often you want risk scoring to run (e.g. weekly).
- Adjust the thresholds in Compute Bus-Factor Risk Scores to match your org's risk appetite (contributor count, commit concentration cutoffs).
- Configure Anthropic credentials for the Claude risk-assessment agent and select the intended model in the Anthropic chat model sub-node.
- Add ticketing-system API credentials and adjust the create/update endpoint, payload, and task matching fields.
- Connect Slack credentials and choose the channel that should receive bus-factor task notifications.

## Push event intake

Receives GitHub push webhooks and normalizes each commit into the shared ownership-signal format before sending it into the common ingestion stream.

## Pull request intake

Receives pull_request (merged) webhooks and converts author/reviewer activity into the workflow's canonical ownership-signal structure.

## Contributor baseline intake

On a schedule, pulls the org's repository list and per-repo contributor stats from GitHub, then normalizes them so they can be scored together with the event-driven signals.

## Buffer normalized signals

Combines the normalized ownership signals from all three intake lanes and posts each into the external buffer service for later batch processing.

## Fetch batch window

Starts the scheduled risk-analysis cycle and retrieves ownership signals accumulated in the buffer during the most recent processing window.

## Score and route

Groups buffered signals by repo/component, computes commit-concentration and active-contributor counts, and routes ambiguous cases toward AI review while sending clear-cut healthy or critical cases down the direct path.

## Resolve ambiguous clusters

Uses a Claude-powered agent to judge borderline ownership-concentration clusters (context matters: is this a real bus-factor risk or an acceptable low-churn component?), then applies the AI result back to the workflow's cluster structure.

## Pass clear clusters

Handles clusters that were already unambiguous (clearly healthy or clearly critical), preserving them without sending them through the AI resolution branch.

## Merge risk outputs

Recombines the AI-resolved ambiguous clusters and the directly passed clear clusters into one unified risk-result stream.

## Create tasks and notify

Builds knowledge-transfer/documentation tasks from the critical-risk clusters, creates or updates them in the ticketing system, and notifies engineering leadership in Slack.
